items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I did copy the way he played 'I've Been Down So Long', because I was learning the trumpet and it was something to help me learn the horn better.

ctx.x: Carpenter started showing me different things concerning phrases on the trumpet and I've always considered him my first teacher although he was not teaching me to read music. Theodore had travelled with many carnival shows and told me many things about the places he had been. His mother lived in Cincy and at the time when I met him, he was living on Richmond Street which was not far from where I had lived with Aunt Mary. It was on the corner of Richmond Street and Mound Streets that I used to go get beer for my…

It was at Carpenter's house that I heard my first Victor record. It was by a trumpet-player named Johnny Dunn and the side I remember was a blues called "I've Been Down So Long". The second line was: "Until down don't worry me".

I can not describe Johnny Dunn's style, but I had not heard anyone play the way he did. In fact I had not heard too many trumpet players except Dolly and Dyer Jones, Sydney de Paris, John Nesbit, Freddie Jenkins and the fellow from New Orleans that played around town on a wagon. There were mostly cornet players in the marching bands but they never played jazz and I listened to these bands and heard all the musicians as anyone else who loved music.
